title: A 60% win rate was below breakeven on this NQ strategy
author: person-person12
selftext:
I keep seeing win rate used as if it tells you whether a strategy is any good. The numbers from one NQ test show how much it leaves out.

I rebuilt the Powell 10am setup in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading), which I own, and ran the mechanical version from July 2023 to February 2026 on one NQ contract. It took 535 trades and won 60.2% of them. The average winner was $522 and the average loser was $806.

With that payoff, the strategy needed to win about **60.7% just to break even on those average outcomes**. It came in at 60.2%, finished with a 0.98 profit factor and lost $3,675. Half a percentage point separated the attractive headline from a negative result.

Its like a coin that lands heads six times out of ten, except tails costs more than heads pays. Counting how often you win hides the part that empties the account.

This was one mechanical interpretation of a discretionary setup, and historical results dont predict the next run. Win rate only becomes useful once the size of the winners and losers sits beside it.
